description.en: Our home and its faithful companion — the world beneath your feet and the Moon that shapes our nights and tides.
description.hr: Nas dom i njegov vjerni pratilac — svijet pod tvojim nogama i Mjesec koji oblikuje nase noci i plime.

back.en: About 4.5 billion years old — formed from the same cloud of dust and gas as the rest of the Solar System.
back.hr: Oko 4,5 milijardi godina — nastala iz istog oblaka prasine i plina kao i ostatak Suncevog sistema.

back.en: Sunlight scatters off air molecules, and blue light scatters the most. The same effect turns sunsets red.
back.hr: Sunceva svjetlost se rasprsuje na molekulama zraka, a plava se rasprsuje najvise. Isti efekt cini zalaske crvenim.

back.en: The leading theory of the Moon's origin: a Mars-sized body slammed into the young Earth, and the debris coalesced into the Moon.
back.hr: Vodeca teorija o nastanku Mjeseca: tijelo velicine Marsa se sudarilo s mladom Zemljom, a otpaci su se spojili u Mjesec.

back.en: The rise and fall of ocean water, caused mainly by the Moon's gravity pulling on Earth's seas as it orbits.
back.hr: Dizanje i spustanje razine mora, uzrokovano uglavnom gravitacijom Mjeseca koja povlaci Zemljine oceane dok kruzi oko nje.

front.en: How big is the Moon compared to Earth?
front.hr: Koliko je Mjesec velik u odnosu na Zemlju?

back.en: About one quarter of Earth's diameter — unusually large for a moon, which is why it can cause total solar eclipses.
back.hr: Oko cetvrtine Zemljinog promjera — neobicno velik za mjesec, zato moze uzrokovati potpuna pomracenja Sunca.

back.en: Yes — it drifts away from Earth by about 3.8 cm every year, roughly the speed your fingernails grow.
back.hr: Da — udaljava se od Zemlje oko 3,8 cm godisnje, otprilike brzinom kojom rastu nokti.

back.en: The layers of gas surrounding Earth. It shields us from radiation, burns up meteors, and keeps our climate livable.
back.hr: Slojevi plinova koji okruzuju Zemlju. Stite nas od zracenja, spaljuju meteore i odrzavaju nasu klimu zivom.

front.en: Why does the Moon look bigger near the horizon?
front.hr: Zasto Mjesec izgleda veci blizu horizonta?

back.en: It's an optical illusion — the Moon isn't actually closer or larger. Your brain just judges its size differently near landmarks.
back.hr: To je opticka iluzija — Mjesec zapravo nije ni blizi ni veci. Tvoj mozak samo drugacije procjenjuje njegovu velicinu blizu orijentira.

back.en: An invisible shield generated by Earth's molten core. It deflects solar wind and dangerous cosmic radiation.
back.hr: Nevidljivi stit koji stvara Zemljina rastopljena jezgra. Odbija Suncev vjetar i opasno kosmicko zracenje.

front.en: How long does the Moon take to orbit Earth?
front.hr: Koliko Mjesecu treba da obidje Zemlju?

back.en: About 27.3 days to complete one orbit, but 29.5 days between full moons — Earth moves too, so the Moon has to catch up.
back.hr: Oko 27,3 dana za jedan krug, ali 29,5 dana izmedju punih mjeseci — Zemlja se takodjer krece, pa Mjesec mora sustici.

front.en: How long will the Apollo footprints last on the Moon?
front.hr: Koliko ce dugo trajati Apollo otisci na Mjesecu?

back.en: Possibly millions of years — with no wind or water to erode them, only rare micrometeorite impacts slowly wear them away.
back.hr: Mozda milionima godina — bez vjetra i vode koji bi ih izbrisali, samo ih rijetki udari mikrometeorita polako trose.

front.en: How fast is Earth spinning, and why don't we feel it?
front.hr: Kojom brzinom se Zemlja vrti i zasto to ne osjecamo?

back.en: About 1,670 km/h at the equator. You don't feel it because everything moves with you — atmosphere included.
back.hr: Oko 1.670 km/h na ekvatoru. Ne osjecas to jer se sve krece s tobom — ukljucujuci atmosferu.
